findings.claim: The observed window is the native endpoint-coordinate score clock [0.0,0.5] with 50 observed score nodes; labels are recorded affinities removed with an equal score prior, so no absolute affinity target is available and all coordinate contrasts are relative, not physical interaction energies.

Continuous contrast functions over the complete observed support are non-monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass shows 4 sign changes with first_rate_z +9.27 and last_rate_z -10.00, and landmark_00_local_dy shows 6 sign changes with first_rate_z -72.37 and last_rate_z +5.52. A constant rule is therefore not supported; a time-conditioned rule is indicated, but no polynomial was accepted and extrapolation is disallowed.

Fit fidelity is weak for several local-derivative features (relative_node_RMSE 0.67-0.78 for landmark_00_local_dx/dy), so their rate changes are low-confidence; soft_mass has lower RMSE (0.29) but still 1 strong sign conflict.

Branch-adjusted covariance contrasts are mostly null: global_centroid_x/y/z have CIs spanning zero (q 0.69-0.97). Only shape_yy reaches nominal p=0.048 with negative whole-window mean and 0.79 same-sign batch fraction, but its q=0.153 does not survive multiplicity adjustment, so no coordinate hypothesis is supported by point estimates alone.

The supplied evidence does not include decoded terminal labels or independent survival/quality credit for the current study; last-record or selection-node enrichment cannot be presented as final affinity benefit, and the immediate-versus-descendant comparison is unavailable.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned sign flip on soft_mass contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: No sign change in the soft_mass contrast when re-estimated on held-out batches, or relative_node_RMSE not improved over a constant rule.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass contrast curve over observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast on landmark_00_soft_mass (early positive rate, late negative rate) may express a within-window directional preference that a constant rule cannot.

hypotheses.falsifier: shape_yy q-value remains above the multiplicity threshold or same-sign batch fraction falls toward 0.5 in additional batches.
hypotheses.statement: Negative shape_yy covariance contrast may indicate a coherent joint-shape coupling rather than an isolated marginal descriptor.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or independent survival/quality credit are supplied, so immediate selection evidence cannot be compared with descendant outcome and last-record credit is not final affinity benefit.
No absolute affinity target exists (recorded affinities removed, equal score prior); all contrasts are relative coordinate contrasts, not physical interaction energies or neural-module causation.
Continuous-trend fits are non-polynomial with weak RMSE for local-derivative features; no extrapolation beyond the observed window is permitted.
Branch-adjusted covariance contrasts are largely null after multiplicity adjustment; no coordinate hypothesis is supported by point estimates alone.
No current-study outcome data are available to the Analyst, so no reward recipe or intervention can be validated here.
